name: Conversation designer
limitedData: This pay is for ads citing conversational AI, which includes engineers, so it probably overstates what designers earn.

ai.reason: Demand is uncertain: the work is shaped by AI products, which also automate parts of it.

skills.why: You write the words people read in an interface, which is the core of designing a conversation.
You design how a person moves through a task, and a conversation is a task with turns.
You test with real people, and conversation designers do the same with transcripts.
You decide what comes first and what comes next.

routes: There is no single route. The article describes designers who came from sales, botany, marketing and Salesforce administration.
The author says the field has less of an established path than mature industries. He recommends building a portfolio, because employers want to see a record of your work.
Knowing how the technology works helps you design within what it can do.
waysIn.caveat: This rests on one blog post by the co-founder of a conversation design software company. It was first published in 2022 and last changed in February 2024.

ai.reason: Drafting specs and analysis is exposed. Prioritising and negotiating with stakeholders needs judgement.

skills.why: You already weigh what to build first, which is the heart of product management.
You bring different teams to one decision, which is most of the job.
You start from what users need, as good product managers do.
You read the numbers behind a decision.

routes: A degree is not essential, and graduates can apply for a first product manager job without any product experience.
It is common to move across from another role, such as marketing or experience design. Employers value transferable skills from other projects.
There is no standard entry route. One university guide says the most important thing is experience in the industry you want to manage a product in.

ai.reason: The government's 2023 study ranks marketing associate professionals twentieth. Positioning is less exposed than campaign production.

skills.why: You understand what a product is for and who it is for, which is positioning.
You know what customers say and do, the evidence behind good messaging.
You write clearly for a reader in a hurry.
You line up product, sales and design around one story.

routes: You may be able to apply directly if you have experience in sales management, advertising, communications or public relations.
Another route is to start as a marketing executive, then gain a qualification from a professional body such as the Chartered Institute of Marketing.
waysIn.caveat: We found no source specific to product marketing, so these are the routes into marketing management in general.

ai.reason: Fieldwork, workshops and cross-team negotiation are hard to automate. Mapping and synthesis are exposed.

You already blueprint services, showing the front and back stage that service design joins up.
You run sessions that get a group to agree, which service design depends on.

You work across teams, as services always do.

routes: Routes listed include a degree or postgraduate study in design innovation, service design, computer science, software development or business design.

pay.ads: 1,097 delivery manager job ads, used for delivery and project management

ai.reason: The government's 2023 study ranks business and financial project management professionals seventh of all UK occupations.

skills.why: You keep many people moving in the same direction, which is delivery management.
You lead and coach a team, which this role asks of you every day.
You run sessions that turn a plan into agreed steps.
You understand what is being built and why.

routes: A degree is the usual requirement for project management. A business or management degree, or one in the industry you want to work in, helps. Postgraduate project management qualifications are open to graduates.

The APM Project Fundamentals Qualification is an introductory qualification. Heriot-Watt University teaches it over two days, followed by a one-hour, 60-question exam. No prior experience is needed. The course page lists 600 pounds plus the exam fee, with no date on the price.

sources.label: My World of Work: project manager
Heriot-Watt University: APM Project Fundamentals Qualification

waysIn.caveat: These sources cover project management. We found none specific to delivery management in digital teams.

ai.reason: Synthesis and note-taking are exposed. Recruiting, interviewing and judgement are less so.

skills.why: You already run research, so this role is the closest to your current work.
You test designs with people and report what you saw.
You run sessions and interviews that draw out what people think.
You combine what people say with what the numbers show.

routes: You can apply directly to user research or digital design companies, or through a specialist agency. You need experience of user-centred design, running research sessions and presenting findings.
Volunteering in research sessions and user interviews is suggested, especially if you do not have a degree.

ai.reason: The government's 2023 study ranks actuaries, economists and statisticians sixth of all UK occupations.

skills.why: You already read data to judge whether a design works.
You turn observations into findings, the same skill with different data.
You organise information so others can find it.

routes: Degrees in statistics, maths, economics, operational research or psychology are listed. Other degrees may work if statistics was part of the course.
Junior roles may be possible after college courses in maths, statistics, computing or economics, or a T Level in digital data analytics.
A Level 4 data analyst apprenticeship exists. One career story on the page applied for it while working as an analyst in a finance team.
waysIn.caveat: These are routes for new entrants. We found no source on moving across from experience design.

ai.reason: The government's 2023 study flags authors and writers as high-automation. Research, structure and policy judgement are less exposed.

skills.why: You write the words inside products, which is the heart of content design.
You decide what goes where and in what order.
You test whether the words work for real people.
You write for everyone, including people using assistive technology.

routes: There is no set path. A content designer writing in 2020 says most of the content designers she spoke to had moved sideways from another role, often journalism, marketing, communications, publishing or editorial work.
Transferable skills include writing, editing, user research, accessibility and information architecture. The article says the tools you know matter less than the practice and ideas you bring.

Government's June 2026 skills update says 7 of the 8 content design skills are shared with graphic, interaction and service design. The one specific to content design is content management and architecture.
waysIn.caveat: The first source is a guest article from 2020 and reflects one person's view of other designers' routes.

name: Accessibility specialist
limitedData: This pay is for any ad citing accessibility, which is a skill and not a job title, so it covers a wide mix of roles.

ai.reason: Automated checks cover only part of accessibility. Testing with people and advising teams stay human work.

skills.why: You already design with accessibility in mind, which this role makes your whole job.
You test with people, including people who use assistive technology.
You can read the code to see why something fails.
You know that fixing a component fixes it everywhere.

routes: A credential is not required to start. BOIA says real-world experience is the most important asset, and that you need to show a basic knowledge of the fundamentals.

The International Association of Accessibility Professionals (IAAP) offers two certificates. CPACC covers broad accessibility knowledge and is not technical. WAS is technical, tests knowledge of WCAG and assumes coding skills.
Exams cost between 385 and 530 US dollars, depending on the certificate and IAAP membership. Check current prices before you plan.
waysIn.caveat: The source is a July 2023 blog from an accessibility consultancy, not the IAAP itself. It also mentions a discounted CPACC rate for people in emerging economies.

name: Front-end developer
limitedData: This pay is for web developer ads in general, not front-end roles specifically.

ai.reason: The government's 2026 assessment describes computer programming as highly exposed to AI automation.

skills.why: You already build in HTML and CSS, which is the base of the job.
You know how interfaces should behave, which helps you build them well.
You work with components, which is how front-end teams build.
You build interfaces that work for everyone.

routes: Routes listed include a foundation degree, HND or degree in web design and development, computer science or similar, and college courses such as the T Level in digital software development.
Apprenticeships are listed, and you may be able to start as a junior developer and train on the job.
waysIn.caveat: The page covers web developers in general, not front-end roles only, and lists routes for new entrants.

ai.reason: The government's 2023 study flags authors and writers as high-automation, and a 2025 Microsoft study finds translators among the most exposed.

skills.why: You write clear instructions that people can follow.
You organise documentation so people can find the answer.
You write for readers with different needs.

routes: There is no fixed route. Employers look for a mix of communication, subject and digital or technical skills, and a postgraduate qualification is not required.

The ISTC accredits courses run by others, for example a five-day programme from Armada and a 14-module online course from Cherryleaf. It also lists free introductory courses and runs no courses itself.
A portfolio from internships, volunteering or a personal blog or website can strengthen an application.

name: Customer success manager
limitedData: This pay is an average of self-reported salaries, not job ads, so it is not measured the same way as the other careers.

ai.reason: A 2025 Microsoft study finds sales and customer service roles highly exposed, but relationship-led account work less so.

skills.why: You manage relationships with people who depend on your work.
You use usage data to spot who needs help.
You see the whole customer journey, not one screen.

routes: No specific degree is required, though some employers prefer one in business, marketing or communications.
The suggested way in is entry-level roles in customer service or account management.
Certifications are optional but can show commitment, for example from the Customer Success Association.
waysIn.caveat: This rests on one undated guide.

name: Learning experience designer
limitedData: Only 13 job ads were found, and the upper end of pay is not reported, so treat this figure with caution.

ai.reason: The government's 2023 study ranks further education teaching professionals and vocational trainers among the most exposed to language-model AI.

skills.why: You design sessions that help a group learn something.
You explain things clearly in few words.
You design the steps a learner moves through.
You test whether people can actually follow what you made.

routes: One qualification route in learning and development is the CIPD Level 5 Associate Diploma. Dumfries and Galloway College lists entry as some HR experience or a degree.
The course averages 12 to 15 months (the maximum is 18), with seven assignments and no exams. It leads to roles that include L&D designer.

sources.label: Dumfries and Galloway College: CIPD Level 5 diploma

waysIn.caveat: This rests on one college course page. We found no guide to how learning designers usually enter, and the course price is not stated.
